versions.name: RXV2-0.9.461-tick-fix
versions.notes: Selector bars: the live red tick now actually shows (a display bug hid it); bigger junction handles that claim the touch so iOS can't turn a drag into a scroll.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.460-six-sections
versions.notes: Bank & Rates selectors, refined (Malcolm): the bar now shows the live red tick with its microsecond value; the junctions between sections can be DRAGGED to resize them; and there are six sections (Rotorflight's six profiles) - sections 5 and 6 start zero-width at the top, drag them open if you need them. Under the hood each section is its own adjustment ('inside this section, profile = N'), so any widths are honoured exactly.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.459-one-bar
versions.notes: Bank and Rates rows on Transmitter channels now carry ONE bar divided into four sections (Malcolm: Rotorflight's three-bar adjustments are baffling) with the live red line and the current section lit green.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.458-portable-backups
versions.notes: Backups travel (Malcolm's idea): Share backup file hands the whole setup to the phone's share sheet - email or AirDrop it to another phone, or to a friend with the same helicopter; Import a backup file adopts it as the model's restore point, then Restore writes it. The file carries everything, including the bank/rates switch selectors the flight controller cannot read back (now declared to the app when saved, restored verbatim). Needs app 3.21 / 3.13.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.457-jumbo-msp
versions.notes: Big flight-controller replies now arrive whole: MSP jumbo frames (0xFF + 16-bit length) reassembled into 640-byte buffers - the 588-byte adjustment table (bank/rates selectors) can be read back and verified, not just written.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.456-bank-rate-switches
versions.notes: Bank (PID profile) and Rates selectors, 4 positions each, from the phone: pick their channels on Transmitter channels (they may share one channel), Save writes them as Rotorflight adjustment ranges (proven live on the Goblin770 - top position = bank 4); the Switches page shows four blue zones with the live red marker AND the flight controller's own answer ('Flight controller: Bank 3') as you flip.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.455-wizard-logo
versions.notes: The wizard has a face: Malcolm's light-hearted wizard-with-helicopter logo now heads the Wizards hub and the New-helicopter checklist.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.454-restart-to-apply
versions.notes: ESC telemetry verdict (proven live: 40.0C flowing on the Goblin770): the wizard could do it all along - features simply apply at BOOT. Saving features now offers the flight-controller restart on the spot, and Before-you-start is back to its three honest tasks (the Ports-tab task was a wrong diagnosis, withdrawn).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.453-esc-port-truth
versions.notes: Before-you-start gains task 4 (found on the first real build): ESC telemetry cannot be fully enabled from the phone - the Ports tab must name which UART the ESC's data wire uses. The First-time basics tick now says so too.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.452-tidy-wiring
versions.notes: Wiring page tidied: the brand-new-board card is gone - that story now lives on the Before-you-start page (wizard step 1).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.451-before-you-start
versions.notes: New 'Before you start' page (Malcolm's wording): the one USB session per new helicopter, as three numbered cards - update the firmware; check the serial port on the Configuration tab matches where the receiver is plugged; enable Telemetry on the Receiver tab then Save & Reboot (bottom right). Wizard step 1 opens it.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.450-computer-session-first
versions.notes: Wizard step 1 is now the one-time computer session, right at the top: turn Telemetry ON and set the serial input to the UART you are using (Save restarts the board); update firmware too while you're there. Everything after is phone-only.
